one_star_reviews.text:
My experience was very negative.
I booked an appointment at the center for the recommended MBST sessions. They gave me a free consultation to explain what it involved. I went on the scheduled day and time. I was attended to by a very polite and friendly young man.
I thought about it and accepted the schedule for the 9 treatment sessions, and I went on the first day at the assigned time.
But to my surprise, when I approached the counter and told the young man why I was there, he immediately presented me with the invoice for the 9 sessions and the machine, demanding I pay the total cost of the treatment (€1650) by card, which I refused to do.
I was so disappointed that I left.
The logical thing, it seems to me, would be to pay for each session individually.

Or even a partial payment; or a deposit. But the total amount before even starting?! I thought it was terrible.

Besides, I had already asked them by email what the payment method was. I went there with great enthusiasm to see if my knees would improve, and they stole that hope from me.
Good service if you pay privately, but if you go through your own insurance... that's a different story!

I am very unhappy with this center. The exercises they have recommended to me are very generic for any injury to this joint. As for the equipment, it is very scarce and they put you in it for very few minutes. They give you an 8-minute massage every three sessions. They recommend you pay to get more attention, and the price goes up to almost €40 for half an hour (this with a 5-session subscription). They make you lie on the stretcher without a paper underneath or anything, and you put your mouth where the last person put their ass. Contacting them is very difficult. They offer you contact via WhatsApp, but an AI answers you. The phone number is not specific to each center and, in addition, it is very difficult to get it answered. In short, it is a rehabilitation center like a delicatessen.

one_star_reviews.text:
I'm giving it one star because I can't give it less.

I DO NOT recommend anyone have their pregnancy monitored at this clinic. They ruin such an important life experience with the poor treatment you receive. The service is terrible: phone support is impossible; no matter what time you call, they don't answer. They'll do their best to give you a one-minute "visit" if they even call, and then they'll ask for your insurance card number.

At each visit, I've spent more time in the waiting room (at least 30 minutes) only to receive a five-minute visit at most. The treatment is completely impersonal and inadequate, with minimal explanations. The doctor is competent, but nothing special; she doesn't inspire confidence, making you feel like just another number. In the end, they're only interested in appointments and billing the insurance companies, and this is perfectly clear with the "coordinator," Lali, who only wants to sell products and pills and see if you're going to give birth privately or not. She's not interested in anything except you accepting what she says, and she doesn't take your preferences into account.

Oh! And with the same test results from the public health system, I'm still waiting for them to tell me about my risk of preeclampsia during pregnancy.

The worst center to have something as important as a pregnancy handled.

one_star_reviews.text:
BEWARE OF THEM!
After going for a couple of years, the moment I canceled a treatment, they stopped being friendly. I've been insisting for three months for a refund, and they just keep giving me the runaround. Neither Mónica nor anyone from Dorsia is taking responsibility. SHAMELESS!

My experience with the director, Mónica, has been truly disappointing.

Throughout the entire process, she constantly tried to convince me to continue, and when I decided against it, she personally assured me that my €370 refund would be processed quickly. However, when it came time to return the money, her response was that she had nothing to do with the refund.

So, what was the point of assuring me that it would be refunded quickly if, when a problem arises, she completely washes her hands of it?

I feel deceived and disappointed because, in my opinion, a person should keep their word, especially when dealing directly with a customer. I've had to call and complain repeatedly to get something as basic as my own money refunded.

My impression is that while they try to attract the customer and get them to sign up, everything is easy and full of promises, but when you decide not to continue and want your money back, the situation changes completely.

To me, this demonstrates a lack of professionalism and consideration for the customer that I find unacceptable.

I would never contract anything with Dorsia again and, after my experience, I wouldn't recommend them either.

A terrible experience with Dorsia.

After paying €370 as a deposit, I decided not to proceed and requested a refund on August 10th. Since then, it's been nothing but problems, waiting, and phone calls to get something as simple as my own money back. It took them a month and a half to process the refund.

What I find completely unacceptable is having to constantly chase the company, calling repeatedly and demanding information about a refund I requested weeks ago.

Every time I contacted them, I had to ask again what was happening, when I would get my money back, and what the status of the process was. This situation creates a completely unnecessary sense of helplessness and exhaustion.

We're talking about €370 that are mine, not a favor the company is doing me. If I fulfill my obligations and pay on time, I expect the same from the company when it's time to refund my money.

After this experience, I have zero confidence in Dorsia. I don't think this is a serious or professional way to treat a customer.

Of course, I wouldn't do anything with Dorsia again, nor would I recommend this company. My experience with their refund process was terrible, and I sincerely hope no one else has to go through the same ordeal to get their money back.

one_star_reviews.text:
I am contacting you, first and foremost, with respect and without any intention of offending, questioning your professionalism, or filing a complaint. I simply need to document how we experienced the last days of our dog Coco's life and how we felt about the care he received at your clinic.

We were on vacation in Torredembarra when Coco, our 15-year-old Yorkshire Terrier, began to feel unwell. As he was an older dog and, moreover, practically blind, we were very worried and decided to take him immediately to a local veterinary clinic, trusting that they would be able to assess what was wrong.
I, Xavi, took him on August 6th. I fully understand that there were no appointments available at that time and that you had to continue with your work. Even so, Coco's assessment was very brief: his temperature was taken, his mouth was superficially examined by lifting his lip, and we were told that he appeared to have inflammation or an infection in his mouth. He was given an anti-inflammatory, and we were told that if he didn't improve in a couple of days, we should call to schedule an appointment.
We trusted that advice. We didn't seek a second opinion or take him to another veterinarian because, quite simply, we had no reason to doubt what we had been told. We thought Coco had a problem with his mouth and that he would improve with the treatment.

However, the next day, Coco worsened. He stopped eating, and we called again to schedule an appointment. We were told they couldn't see him until the following Tuesday. When we explained that Coco wasn't eating, they told us we could pick up Royal Canin Recovery food to feed him with a syringe until the appointment.
We did so. During those days, we did everything we could to keep him hydrated and fed, but Coco didn't make it to the Tuesday appointment. He passed away in the early hours of Sunday morning.

I know perfectly well that no one can know if a different examination, an earlier visit, or a different diagnosis would have changed the outcome. Coco was 15 years old and a very old dog. I don't intend to state something I can't know, nor do I blame anyone for his death.

But I did want to convey something that has been very difficult for us to accept: we would have liked to feel that, having a 15-year-old dog in front of us, practically blind and unwell, his situation had been assessed with a little more depth and sensitivity. Perhaps the possibility of bringing the visit forward could have been considered, or at least we could have been told more clearly that if he worsened or stopped eating, we should go to an emergency room or look for another option.

We trusted the initial assessment precisely because we trusted a professional. That's why we didn't think it was necessary to take him elsewhere. And now, after his passing, we're left with the feeling that perhaps we should have done something more, even though at the time we acted thinking we were doing the right thing.

Coco wasn't just a dog to us. He had been part of our family for many years and was a member of our household. Therefore, although I fully understand that a veterinary clinic can be busy and that it's not always possible to see every animal immediately, I believe that in cases of very old animals in a delicate state, it's important to be especially sensitive and assess whether the situation requires more urgent attention.

I'm not writing this letter to create conflict, but because I needed to express how we felt and because I believe our experience can help another animal in a similar situation receive a more thorough assessment or faster guidance.
Coco passed away at 15 years old, and we were with him until the very end. We loved him very much and are still trying to come to terms with his loss. I simply wanted you to know how we experienced those last days and to leave a record of our feelings.

one_star_reviews.text: They sell you sick orchids. The first time, I thought it was strange that the orchid I had ordered four days earlier looked suspiciously sick when I went to pick it up, so I said I wasn't taking it and left it there. The second time, I was in a hurry to get a gift for a friend, so I bought an orchid and gave it to her that same day. After four weeks, it started showing strange symptoms. My friend and I went back to the store with the plant, and they downplayed it, saying the plant only needed water. After six weeks, despite following the care instructions on the QR code that came with the plant, its leaves started to yellow. After two months, they continued to yellow and began falling off one by one. My friend left me in charge of the plant I had given her when she went on vacation, and I put it next to mine. I've cared for them the same way. Mine are perfectly fine (I've had them since 2018, and of course, I didn't buy them there), and all that's left of the one I gave my friend are the roots.

Very disappointing experience

I was very disappointed with the customer service at this Women’secret store. I arrived at 9:45 PM, 15 minutes before the advertised closing time of 10:00 PM. The sales assistant refused to let me enter, telling me that they were about to close.

What made the situation even more frustrating is that the store was still full of customers who were browsing, choosing items, and making purchases.

There was also no clearly displayed notice or information stating that customers were not allowed to enter 15 minutes before closing, or that entry was restricted 45 minutes before closing. If there is such a policy, it should be clearly communicated to customers.

I completely understand that staff need time to close the store, but refusing entry 15 minutes before the official closing time, while other customers are still shopping, is very disappointing and unprofessional.

I hope management will review this situation and ensure that customers are treated fairly and that any early-entry restrictions are clearly communicated.

one_star_reviews.text:
Adeslas is simply a disgrace.

My fiancé is facing one of the most difficult moments of his life: he has leukemia and is undergoing treatment. And instead of having peace of mind to take care of his health, we are having to deal with a problem caused by the insurance company itself.

Now, Adeslas is questioning the service and claiming that he already knew he was sick before taking out the insurance. The absurdity is that the leukemia was discovered here in Spain. He was initially seen and investigated for other issues until, after several tests, they finally discovered what was really happening.

He didn't have a hidden pre-existing leukemia diagnosis. The disease was discovered here, during this entire medical investigation process.

And, as if this whole situation wasn't difficult enough, my fiancé and his father were treated in a completely disrespectful way by Adeslas's customer service representatives. At a time when he is sick, debilitated, and fighting cancer, hearing mocking comments and perceiving the lack of willingness to help is simply revolting.

We are not asking for any favors. We are talking about a person with leukemia who needs medical care and follow-up.

While for them this seems to be just a bureaucratic matter, for us there is a person who is unwell, undergoing chemotherapy, and who needs medical assistance.

It is unacceptable that, in such a serious situation, in addition to having to deal with the disease, we also have to fight against the insurance company itself to get care. And even worse is being treated with disrespect and as if the situation were not serious.

If Adeslas has doubts about his medical history, let them investigate and resolve this through the appropriate channels. But it is unacceptable to hinder the care of a person undergoing cancer treatment and then treat the patient and family with mockery and a total lack of empathy.

We are tired, indignant, and above all, worried about his health. A person with leukemia deserves care, respect, and humanity, not to be treated this way.

one_star_reviews.text: After four appointments spaced a month apart, Dr. María Muñoz administered two ozone injections to my right facet joint for back pain, with no improvement whatsoever. I was scheduled for a specific time, but after waiting two hours, they left me waiting in a room for another 30 minutes. Once I received the second injection, Dr. Muñoz simply told me to schedule a follow-up appointment in two weeks. This follow-up consisted of asking how I was feeling; there was no palpation of the area, no need for an ultrasound, X-ray, etc. It lasted three minutes, during which she asked how I was feeling and recommended another ozone injection session on the spot if the pain persisted. This was something one was expected to accept and trust, hoping it might be necessary, and then proceeding out of desperation. If you decide against it and want to reconsider, the supposed follow-up costs €75. Now, two weeks after the last session and €600 spent, I'm exactly the same and have to go to the emergency room for injections. I called the clinic to ask Dr. Muñoz if what I was experiencing was normal, and they scheduled a follow-up appointment with her for €75. I explained that I didn't want a so-called follow-up appointment; I just wanted to know through a phone call if what I was experiencing was normal, since I'd already spent a considerable amount of money and was still in the same situation. They told me the doctor was on vacation and would return in 15 days, at which point they would inform her. So, I'm stuck waiting for nothing, and the service leaves much to be desired. They seem overwhelmed and provide no real human touch, starting from reception. After trusting them and spending a significant amount of money, I perceive the entire process as very sterile and disorganized. I think they're taking my money but not the pain; in fact, I'm worse now, and on top of that, I feel scammed. It's a mystery that you know when you start but not when this supposedly expensive treatment will end without any results. I don't recommend them.

I am Inmaculada García Márquez, a nurse by profession, a senior technician in occupational risk prevention in matters of safety, ergonomics and applied psychosocial factors, in addition to other qualifications such as CAP, and a technician in legionellosis prevention and X-ray operator, etc. On October 2, 2026, I went with my husband to said clinic which "has little or nothing to do with pain." I was seen by a "doctor named Benitez... I don't even want to remember his name, like Miguel de Cervantes put at the beginning of his novel DON QUIXOTE DE LA MANCHA." This supposed "doctor who claims to be a SPECIALIST IN ANESTHESIA AND RESUSCITATION"... didn't even get up from his comfortable barnacle sofa to perform a complete anatomical examination of the spinal condition I've suffered from since an accident 22 years ago, which from the beginning has caused me pain with functional impairment and radicular and dermatomal involvement. During these 22 years, no one has dared to tell me that I have "subjective pain" and that I should barely take any medication! This being, lacking social skills and empathy, should really go back to school or... It's best to leave the profession since I'm unaware of the multiple pain measurement scales we have in healthcare, which I've used as part of my patients' pain management as a nurse. I've personally examined and assessed their musculoskeletal system, distal reflexes, and, of course, pupils, also using scales of consciousness like the Glasgow Coma Scale and the UPJ scale. I have a total disability due to a work accident, granted through the courts, which recognizes my motor impairment due to pain, preventing me from performing any work. It completely prevents me from sleeping properly and being fully independent. I depend on my husband for most household tasks, and I can't do any physical work because my entire spine is affected. I also have pain in my head, upper and lower extremities, and limbs. This prevents me from standing or sitting for extended periods, and I can't even sleep at night. This has been the case since 2019, and I've been getting worse despite treatment from other professionals.

I'm keeping more clinical documents because it's something I don't... Can you even call him a doctor? Unable to review the new evidence I submitted, he wrote to me stating he wants to insert an electrostimulation catheter into my spinal cord after telling me "my pain is subjective." I have a recording of the consultation and, along with reports from other specialists, I reserve the right to take legal action!

It's unbelievable that in the 21st century, a human being, besides being humiliated while sick, continues to suffer pain that prevents them from sleeping or living... and there are couch potatoes who pass judgment without even getting up from their sofas...

one_star_reviews.text:
My experience with IVI has been disappointing.

I want to begin by highlighting that the attention from the administrative staff, nurses, blood draw personnel, and laboratory staff was always excellent. I also acknowledge that, after expressing an initial disagreement, my gynecologist's treatment improved significantly, becoming more approachable and attentive.

However, after completing a Genetic IVF treatment costing €8,723.34, plus additional expenses for complementary tests, medication, travel between Tenerife and Gran Canaria, and accommodation, my final impression is that I didn't find a difference in care that justified the significant investment compared to my previous experience with the public healthcare system.

The main differences I perceived were more modern facilities, faster service, and greater availability for procedures, even on weekends. However, the procedures, medication, and overall approach to treatment seemed very similar to what I had experienced before.

I chose IVI because of its prestige, the trust it inspires as a national leader in assisted reproduction, and the expectation of receiving a highly personalized approach after having previously undergone unsuccessful treatments. Precisely for this reason, I expected a more in-depth analysis of my medical history and a clearly differentiated strategy.

After receiving a negative result, I was instructed to discontinue the medication and scheduled for a future appointment. My feeling was that I did not receive a detailed explanation of the possible causes of the result, nor a thorough analysis of my case.

Subsequently, I filed a formal complaint outlining my experience and requesting a review of the treatment circumstances. The response I received rejected any possibility of a refund and, in my opinion, failed to address several of the issues raised, including the information I received after the negative result, the additional costs incurred during the process, and other aspects outlined in my complaint.

I deeply respect the work of the professionals who treated me and am fully aware that no assisted reproduction treatment can guarantee pregnancy. However, I believe that an investment of this magnitude deserves more comprehensive information, more personalized follow-up, and a more satisfactory response when a patient files a reasoned and documented complaint.

This opinion reflects solely my personal experience as a patient.

This clinic is a disgrace, one mistake after another. I completed my first treatment, and when I was about to start the second, I realized my thyroid had become dislocated due to the hormones they'd given me. I told them I wasn't going to start the second treatment for that reason, and they said the ultrasound they'd done wouldn't be covered by the last or the next treatment, and I'd have to pay for it separately. They didn't even bother to check on me. And that's not to mention that the day my doctor wasn't there, a doctor saw me and told me that since I'd been inseminated, it wasn't going to work that time—a wasted attempt...and a lot of money. They have absolutely no shame and play with people's dreams.

Our experience has been very disappointing. We enrolled our 4-year-old son, informing them from the outset that he attended early intervention programs, and they even spoke with their psychologists before accepting the enrollment.

However, on the second day, they told us he wouldn't be participating in the field trips and that he would be placed with a group of 2-year-olds because, according to them, they didn't have the resources to care for him. The most surprising thing is that, when we enrolled him, they assured us they had plenty of counselors, and then justified their inability to assign one to our son by saying some were absent due to exams.

This situation forced us to withdraw him from the center, leaving us without the summer plans we had already made. If a center cannot meet certain needs, the responsible thing to do is to communicate this before accepting enrollment, not after the child has already started camp.

Given the center's response, I must say I'm not at all surprised that they are complaining about a review rather than the service provided. We want to clarify that our son does not require permanent individualized attention. Furthermore, the professionals familiar with his situation, both at his school and at the Provincial Council, considered it a mistake to place him in a two-year-old group. The problem wasn't that we offered alternatives and they were rejected, but rather that, once the service had begun, the initially communicated conditions were changed, including his exclusion from outings and his placement in a two-year-old group.

About three years ago, I went there to get my hair cut because my usual salon was closed for vacation.

Well, a girl with platinum blonde hair attended to me personally, and, in my opinion, gave me a terrible haircut. I left looking even more disheveled than when I went in.

But here's the kicker: instead of the girl who cut my hair charging me, the owner charged me and, on top of that, ASKED FOR MY PHONE NUMBER.

Honestly, I don't think I should have to give out my personal phone number, especially when they don't explain why it's needed or how they're going to use my information. And, given the result of the haircut, it wasn't surprising they wanted my information in case I left a bad review later.

It was a disgrace.

And this is absolutely true, in case the owner decides to tell me it's not true. After what happened with the phone number, I'm completely fed up.

I DO NOT RECOMMEND IT.

For two and a half years, I've been suffering from problems in my left and right shoulders (calcific tendinitis, etc.) that caused biomechanical imbalances, muscle contractures, and back pain (and, according to a report from Begoña Hospital, "a disabling condition"). My mother initially denied the existence of the problem, but after I came to this clinic, she began to claim it was psychosomatic. Thanks to shockwave therapy, I partially regained mobility in my left arm, and thanks to a calcification lavage, I'm finally healing my left shoulder. As recommended at Begoña Hospital, I want to repeat the lavage technique on my right shoulder, but my mother insists that with psychological treatment, I would reabsorb the calcium without any medical intervention and that this clinic would have helped me regain arm mobility without shockwave therapy. I'd like to know if these outlandish ideas are my mother's own invention or if she picked them up at this clinic.

Updated 03/10/2026

It's not me who's constantly questioning medical criteria, it's my mother.

It's my mother who has been questioning the suitability of the only technique that has allowed me to reabsorb calcium and that can be considered successful in my case (and has been considered as such by doctors and physical therapists) for the past few months.

one_star_reviews.text: I want to formally record the absolute lack of professionalism and ethics at this dental clinic. My experience has been a complete disaster: first, they scheduled me for an examination on a day when the orthodontist wasn't even there. They did the same for a man who came from out of town, wasting his time and money on gas. A few days later, after telling me to come "whenever I could" during their extended Friday hours, I arrived at 2:15 pm and found the clinic locked from the inside because all the staff were having lunch at the same time without any prior notice, leaving me waiting outside for an hour. When they finally gave me the results there, they tried to push a marketing strategy by offering an inflated estimate of €3,400, which they desperately lowered twice in one minute to €2,800 to pressure me without telling them the price at all (they do this to convince me). When I told them my maximum budget was €2,500 and that I couldn't afford it right now, I asked them to send me my X-rays on a USB drive so I could get a second opinion, and that's when the blackmail started. The consultant threatened me in writing that she wouldn't give me the tests "because they were free" and they tried to coerce me by saying their lawyers would charge me for the study retroactively. After researching this and seeing that it's completely illegal, the director (Eduardo) promised to send me everything free of charge. However, they've been using the excuse of a broken hard drive for days to delay the process. It's 8:00 PM and they're still withholding the tests, knowing that I have a crucial doctor's appointment tomorrow at 9:00 AM, which I've already had to postpone twice because of them. It's a lie that they can't export them, since I saw the photos and the scanner working perfectly on their local computer on Friday when they explained the diagnosis to me. As soon as they see you reject their quote, they lose interest.

My experience wasn't good, mainly due to the poor value for money. I had a manicure and pedicure done, and the final price was €68, which I found excessive for the service I received and, especially, for the result.

I wouldn't have minded paying that amount if the experience, the care, and the finish were up to par, but in my case, they weren't. I've been to salons with a higher level of service and better results for similar or even lower prices.

I hate to leave a negative review, but I don't think €68 for a manicure and pedicure with this outcome is justified. Personally, I wouldn't go back.

one_star_reviews.text: We requested a medical examination for the renewal of our firearms license after waiting two hours. We were all scheduled for 12:00 PM, but I arrived at 11:50 AM and there were already at least eight people ahead of me. We waited two hours until they gave us the certificate, and when we went to submit it to the firearms office to complete the process, they told us it wasn't correct. Apparently, when we left the clinic, we had a missed call, which we tried to return about twenty times without success. We left a message on the voicemail asking why they didn't know we had called. To our surprise, when the firearms office told us it wasn't valid, we had to call about thirty more times without getting through. After so many attempts, the physiotherapist finally answered, and we asked him to please tell the women at the door to answer the phone. Once we finally got through to her, they told us that instead of the firearms license and renewal certificate, they had issued us a certificate for getting a motorcycle license. This misplaced document took us two whole days to complete. We are very dissatisfied with the service; they didn't even bother to call back to let us know the certificate was incorrect.

one_star_reviews.text:
⭐ 1 STAR — Very disappointing experience with Neptuno Car Hire

Our rented car would not start because of a battery problem, leaving us stranded. At the time, I did not have the rental contract with me, so I did not have the emergency number available. We had no choice but to call a taxi, if not, my friends would miss their flight.

When I later contacted Neptuno to claim the insurance, the owner told me that I could no longer claim because I should have called the emergency number when the car broke down.

I understand that this may be their procedure, but there is a serious problem: I later tried calling the emergency number myself, even though we no longer needed assistance — and the number was INVALID.

This means that even if I had somehow had the number available and called it when the car broke down, we would apparently still have ended up having to find our own transportation because their emergency number was not working.

I also sent Neptuno an email explaining the situation, but I received no reply.

The most frustrating part is being refused an insurance claim because I didn't follow a procedure that, when I subsequently tried to test it, could not actually be used because the emergency number provided was invalid.

A breakdown can happen with any rental car. What matters is how the rental company responds and supports its customer.

In our case: the car failed, we had to pay for a taxi, the emergency number provided was invalid, our email was ignored, and our insurance claim was rejected.

Very disappointing customer service. I would not rent from Neptuno again.

one_star_reviews.text:
We went to Rapimueble to buy some furniture. At the time of purchase, they informed us that assembly would cost €100, which we initially accepted.

Later, we decided not to hire them for assembly because a family member is perfectly capable of assembling the furniture. It was then that they informed us that delivery would cost €50, as the furniture was coming from Chiclana. Up to that point, no problem.

What we find incredible is that at no point were we informed of the delivery conditions: that the furniture would be left at street level and that it did not include carrying it upstairs or bringing it inside the house.

We believe they should clearly inform customers of the delivery price, the reason for the cost, and the service conditions before they hire them. In our case, we only found out that the furniture would be left on the street during the delivery driver's call, barely 10 minutes before he arrived.

The unbelievable thing isn't that there's a curbside delivery service, but that you only find out 10 minutes beforehand, when they're practically there, and that's all the time you have to go downstairs and take care of the furniture.

If we had known from the beginning that the delivery consisted of leaving the furniture on the street, we could have made arrangements or considered another option.

A rather disappointing experience due to the lack of information and transparency.

one_star_reviews.text:
Modern center with fast initial attention. So far, so good. Unfortunately, our experience with the administrative management was very unprofessional.

We needed to be able to consult some MRIs electronically, not on CD, because an entire Neurology service at Trueta Hospital was waiting for them. At 12:32 p.m. they told us that access would be available along with the report in approximately half an hour.

An hour later, when we called again, another secretary told us that this was not possible and that no one had told us, even though they had previously spoken to the head of service to explain the situation. They assured us that they would call us back in 10 minutes.

Coincidentally, after those 10 minutes there was a shift change. The person who attended to us at the time —no complaints against him, as it was clear and correct— explained to us that it was impossible to have it ready because the radiologist who was supposed to do the report was not there yet and would come in between 3 and 4 p.m. At that time it was already approximately 2:30 p.m.

What is most annoying is not having to wait, but having received contradictory information for two hours, keeping us and an entire Neurology service waiting for something that, apparently, from the beginning could not be ready in the time they had indicated to us.

It would have been much simpler and more professional to tell us from the beginning that he would not be available until the afternoon. In situations of concern and medical uncertainty, transparency and reliable information are especially important.

one_star_reviews.text:
I'm giving it one star because I can't give it less. I came today to get my 11-year-old daughter's eyes checked (she's a minor, of course). A man named Ruben attended to her and took the number so that the person in charge, named "Jesus," could see her while he finished with the other patient. We waited, and they quickly came out. Ruben started working with the client, and then Jesus looked at my daughter and said, "Who am I going to have tested? She doesn't look 11." He grabbed the number and went to see someone else while we waited there, being next in line. I approached a robot that was walking around, a girl who didn't seem to know anything. I told her he was the one who would be testing my daughter, and she said yes, but she was seeing him, but she wasn't going to graduate. I said, "But we were here first!" and she just smiled and shrugged as if she didn't care. Then Ruben approached her, and quickly the gossip and comments started. What I said at the end of 15/20 minutes Jesus comes and my daughter asks him how he sees with the glasses he has and he answers fine and asks me if he is going to take the exam as if that was not what we asked for at the beginning... the girl tells me come in with me mom. And they walk by, and I ask him if I can go in with her, and he tells me to stay by the door in a very rude way. Then he starts asking the girl if she's Paraguayan, if she writes with her right or left hand, if she kicks with her left or right foot. I say, "Excuse me, what do your questions have to do with the exam?" To which he bluntly replies, "Well, it does." I say, "Yes, but can you tell me what it has to do with it, because the girl is a minor?" He simply says, without looking at me and in a rude manner, "Well, it does." So, as a mother, I tell him, "Well, I'm done with the exam, don't continue." My daughter has been taking exams since she was two years old, and no one has ever asked her about her nationality or commented on whether she looks older or younger than her age because of her body, or because she's left-handed or right-handed.
I go outside and tell Ruben I'm not going to continue with the exam for the reasons mentioned above. He also replies, "It has to do with it." I ask him, "Can you explain why?" I said, "No one has ever asked those questions or made those comments before." And as a mother of a As a minor, I have the right to know why, to which he couldn't answer. I asked for a reference number to file a complaint because it felt like harassment, and he said there wasn't one, that I'd get caught. Then he offered me a complaint form and went to tell Jesús, who came and grabbed it, saying I couldn't take it because they didn't have any more and they weren't going to give it to me anyway. He said he was a professional, assuming he knew more than me, which can only be described as bilingual, harassment, and objection to a minor and his mother.

And since they wouldn't let me take the form or give me any information, Ruben didn't give me a number for a minor complaint, saying that (Jesus) is the store manager and there's no one above him... so I have to write it here...

Because I came to get my glasses made and the doctor never asked me the questions he asked an 11-year-old girl. My 14-year-old grandson came and he wasn't asked those questions either.

From Ruben, the girl who just walks around with her hands clasped behind her back, and Jesus...

My daughter has felt harassed and intimidated. I hope the manager of this company takes note of this complaint.

one_star_reviews.text: It's shameful, the doctor doesn't even listen to you and prescribes medication for something you don't have, and doesn't even let you explain.

What a disastrous hospital! They have absolutely no heart and play with the lives of our little ones. All they want is for you to arrive practically with the baby in your arms. I've lost count of how many times they sent us home at 41 weeks and 4 days pregnant, unable to dilate and in a lot of pain, but they don't care. On top of that, the emergency room doctors have no shame, whispering about every single woman who arrives and criticizing all the pain pregnant women are experiencing, implying that all the pain and discomfort our women feel is a lie. Then I really don't like that they leave us alone to go into the hospital and that there are so many restrictions and rules. Less rules, more heart, and less paying taxes for such terrible treatment. Best wishes, and I hope this changes for expectant mothers.

one_star_reviews.text:
Please be very careful if you choose to use this company...
They charged us nearly 60 euros for a pick-up from the airport, and the return trip in an Uber cost less than 15.
The van we were hiring wasn't at the premises when we arrived and when it got there we were given a whistle-stop tour round it inside the small-ish garage.
To be fair, the van ran well and we had a great holiday.
When we returned it at the pre-arranged time and date - a Saturday - the garage was shut. We phoned and were told to just post the keys though the door and go.
We asked for someone to come out and inspect the return with us but were told that wouldn't be possible.
When the van was inspected on the Monday were were invoiced over 600 euros for three repairs that we are absolutely sure were not our fault.
We have tried to reason with GoCamper but have had no joy so we've had to resort to this review.

one_star_reviews.text:
My experience with this clinic since yesterday has been quite frustrating and, frankly, worrying, especially considering it's a mental health service.

I initially contacted them via WhatsApp because I needed a consultation with a psychiatrist, but the responses were unclear, and I eventually had to call. They scheduled a supposed pre-consultation with the medical director. The appointment arrived, and after waiting for over an hour without receiving a call, I had to contact the clinic myself to ask what was happening. They told me she would call me back.

When we finally spoke, I tried to clarify several points about the professional and the service I needed. I specifically asked if it was a psychiatrist, if they were a medical doctor, and if they could prescribe medication. The answers were unclear, and I had to insist several times. Finally, they assured me that they could.

However, during that same conversation, they tried to sell me a package of 10 sessions for a certain price. I still had doubts because my need was very simple: I wanted ONE consultation with a psychiatrist, not to purchase a therapy package. I ended the call feeling like I'd spoken to a salesperson rather than someone responsible for guiding and supporting a patient seeking psychiatric care.

Given the insecurity this whole experience created, I didn't continue the process at that point.

To my surprise, the next day a secretary contacted me again, asking why I hadn't attended the previous day's appointment. This was especially disconcerting considering I was the one who had waited for over an hour and even had to call to get someone to speak to me.

I explained the whole situation again. The receptionist apologized and informed me that the person who had spoken to me had confused the psychology and psychiatry services. She also explained that the price they had quoted me was incorrect and that the 10-session package they had tried to sell me was for psychology. In other words, they had offered me a service I hadn't requested after I had specifically asked if we were talking about psychiatric care.

The receptionist tried to resolve the situation and, as compensation for everything that had happened, offered me a package of three consultations at a more reasonable price. She said she would send me the quote by email so I could proceed with the process. I'm still waiting for that email.

In short: I've spent two days trying to get something as simple as a single consultation with a psychiatrist, which I also needed quite urgently. I've had to call, insist, wait, explain several times what kind of professional I need, receive incorrect information, listen to offers for packages I hadn't requested, and continue waiting for paperwork and quotes without having been able to book an appointment yet.

I understand that mistakes can happen, and I appreciate that the receptionist apologized and tried to find a solution. But when someone contacts a clinic because they need psychiatric care, I believe that care, clarity, and efficiency with the patient should take precedence over business processes and bureaucracy.

My experience so far, unfortunately, has been the exact opposite.

I strongly advise against using MRW for time-sensitive shipments. I paid an extra premium for insured delivery with a strict deadline (August 11). The package arrived 5 days late, long after I had left the city. Instead of proactive problem-solving, MRW’s system falsely logged the package as 'delivered' while it was still sitting in their depot—a fact confirmed by GPS telemetric data and a direct phone call to their staff.

During this delay, I reached out multiple times via their official channels of communication and proactively offered multiple alternative solutions to get the delivery done smoothly (including rerouting and third-party pickup). Customer support via WhatsApp stopped responding entirely when confronted with the evidence. Formal emails to their claims department remain completely ignored to this day.

I only managed to recover my property because I arranged for a third party to do the logistical work MRW was paid to do. There has been zero accountability, zero communication, and no compensation for the breached contract. A textbook example of operational failure.

one_star_reviews.text: I was a patient of Dr. Eugenio Blanes for several years, and a few months ago I decided to stop. I find it absolutely intolerable that he dedicates himself to spreading statements about menopause on social media that can be very harmful and sow anxiety. In consultations, he tells you it's a natural process and barely listens to your symptoms (not just menopausal ones), and then, on social media, he talks about how women are practically disabled when they reach menopause, in addition to creating excessive social alarm with things like increased cardiovascular risk. If women are portrayed as beings who constantly can't "think clearly" or "get on with their lives," we are stigmatized, job opportunities are closed to us, we are socially marginalized, and women are blamed for everything because, of course, they are nervous/sad/whatever because they are menopausal. There's a difference between raising awareness and pathologizing and stigmatizing. It seems that ever since they bought the regenerative laser machine, they don't know how to recoup their investment. Dr. Eugenio Blanes: listen to the symptoms of the women who come to your office instead of spreading alarm on social media by listing all the possible symptoms. And, by the way, men with a waist circumference greater than 94 centimeters also have a much higher cardiovascular risk.

A few months ago, my partner and I had our first couples therapy session with this center and, honestly, it was one of the worst experiences we have ever had in terms of the quality of the service.
During the session, we explained the situation we were experiencing at the time, but the therapist did not know how to approach it or conduct the session professionally. The session was very uncomfortable, since she practically did not know what to say to us and limited herself to asking us to ask her questions. We did, but even in these situations she herself did not know what to answer or how to guide us.
In addition, the session lasted approximately 40 minutes, although, as we had been informed, the sessions lasted 50 minutes.
After discussing our experience with people around us and with other professionals, we agreed that what had happened was not a couples therapy session that met the minimum expectations that we expected from a professional service. For this reason, we contacted the center to file a complaint.
Initially, we perceived a lot of interest from the center in wanting to resolve our dissatisfaction. However, the proposals they offered us seemed inadequate to us, such as taking an online course. At no point initially was a solution proposed to us that we considered proportional to the service received. Later, however, the possibility of a refund was mentioned by us due to our dissatisfaction with the quality of the service.
When we formally requested this refund, we were informed that they would consult with Silvia Congost herself and that they would later give us an answer.
7 months have passed and we still have not received any response from the center and, obviously, without having received any refund of the money.
We consider that this situation demonstrates a very important lack of seriousness and professionalism, especially considering that it is a center dedicated precisely to the field of therapy and couple relationships.
After this experience, we decided to go to another therapist and the difference has been abysmal. The session with this professional had absolutely nothing to do with the one we received at this center: she knew how to listen to us, conduct the session, ask the right questions and give us tools and guidance. With that, I must say that the session with her lasted almost 120 minutes. No point of comparison.
Therefore, our experience with this center has been very negative. It may have a lot of reputation and recognition, but, at least in our case, the experience we had has not been at all consistent with the image of professionalism that they transmit.
Therefore, as I have mentioned, from our experience, we will never be able to have good words for Silvia Congost's center.

I'm going to be clear in this review.

The professionals do a good job, and overall, everything is fine, except for one aspect that I find quite important.

When you ask about the treatments, they explain that you have to take dutasteride and minoxidil for life. What no one explains clearly is that if, for any reason, you stop being a client of the company, they stop providing you with the prescriptions necessary to continue the treatment.

This seems especially serious to me because we're talking about a long-term treatment. If you interrupt the medication, you could lose some or all of the hair that the treatment had managed to maintain.

I believe this information should be explained from the beginning, without the client having to specifically ask about it. If they're offering you a treatment that's meant to be maintained for life, I think both the company and the professionals who treat you should clearly inform you what happens to the medication and prescriptions if you ever stop being a client.

My criticism, therefore, is directed both at the company's policy and at the lack of information I received from the staff. I believe this is too important for the client to have to figure it out on their own afterward.

I ordered a hall stand (an 85x15 cm shelf with a 25x25 cm cube module) on October 24, 2025, paying the €100 deposit indicated in the quote for a total of €200. At that time, I was verbally told that the approximate delivery time would be a couple of months (already a long time for such a small order). Well, it turns out the furniture has only just been delivered, that is, almost 10 MONTHS!! for a shelf that's 85 cm by 15 cm wide. Seriously, look at the attached photos to understand what we're talking about.

And the worst part wasn't even the wait; it was two very unprofessional things: the condition of the furniture upon delivery and the lack of attention and explanation I received regarding the situation. Calls and WhatsApp messages every so often asking about the status went unanswered. If you're not capable or can't handle a job, don't accept it. I find this incredibly unprofessional. And if you're not even capable of doing a good job, at least provide adequate customer service. It's unacceptable that I've been chasing him for months with messages and calls and haven't even received a single WhatsApp reply. How long does it take to get a response like "It's not ready yet, I hope by X"? Nothing. It's impossible to reach him or get a delivery date. Of course, I was the one who had already paid €100 upfront. I even started to wonder if it was a scam.

To top it all off, after spending 10 months on this project, I'd be ashamed to deliver the furniture in that condition. You can see the photos; it's covered in dirt and scratches—a brand new piece of furniture. At least have the decency to deliver something presentable.

I understand that projects can experience delays, but 10 months for a project of this nature, the lack of communication, and the condition in which it was finally delivered don't seem like a professional way to work. Based on my experience, I wouldn't hire them again, much less recommend them to anyone.

This morning I took bus number 2 and went to pay by card, but it wasn't working. I tried again with another card, and still nothing; the card reader wasn't working.
The driver asked if I didn't have cash, and I said no. I tried again, and it still didn't work. I told the driver if he wanted, I could get off and pay his colleague on the other bus that was right next to us, and he said no.
He said he'd let us go to the stadium if the card reader wasn't working there due to lack of coverage. I told him the other bus goes to Carrefour, and he said it would drop us off behind it. We went to the other bus, and he told us that one didn't go to Carrefour.
What a disaster!

And all because the card reader wasn't working.
I wanted to pay, even if it was on another bus, even if it wasn't that one. We got off, and another bus number 2 arrived in no time, just a few minutes later, and the driver was so kind, and the card reader worked on the first try.
What a lack of human compassion.

A great doctor, a real chatterbox (I don't remember his name, but I know he talked a lot), convinced me to get them fixed. Since I'm a bit of a mess, I decided to get removable dentures. Okay, so they took out the bad ones, great. The dentist fixed the front teeth, great. The doctor I'm talking about only knew how to sand and sand, and when he realized it, he'd eaten a piece of the tooth. Well, he told me that when we finished, we'd see what he could do. There was nothing there; that gap was left empty. When it was fine, the second set of dentures they gave me wasn't good. I didn't like how much metal was visible, and the inner part, the part that goes against the palate, wasn't glued on. I ran my tongue over it and cut myself. I put it up. I'm telling you about their decision regarding the metal brackets, which are very visible, that they should paint them with nail polish, and that the palate part is fine, that I should only wear it for eating. I've spent almost 3000 euros to have the dentures stored away, and I'm not even finished yet. I still need the gum cleaning, which they haven't contacted me about, and I'm not going to go back to get that done. I don't know how they'll be able to reimburse me, but honestly, everything seemed great, and it all turned out to be the worst experience and the worst money spent.

one_star_reviews.text: I went to the doctor one morning when I was eight weeks pregnant, and she was super nice and friendly. Today I had a rather unpleasant and sad experience. We arrived seven minutes late, walking in at 5:37 pm when our appointment was at 5:30 pm. I apologized because it was raining and there was a lot of traffic. I was with my family when she told me we were late. I told her I didn't mind waiting while she saw a woman I was with, or even waiting for her to have her ultrasound, since I understood I was late. She very rudely told me I was interrupting and accused me of speaking to her rudely, which was not the case at all. I felt very sorry for her because I work in healthcare and face-to-face interactions with the public, and that was completely untrue. My family was quite surprised by her comment and had to explain to her that it hadn't been like that. So we went into the ultrasound room, feeling quite anxious and sad, and with very little desire to do it. People who work with the public, especially with vulnerable individuals like pregnant women and those experiencing hormonal changes, should be a bit more sensitive, even if it was just for being seven minutes late. She performed the ultrasound, and for me, it was a very uncomfortable situation after everything that had happened, as it's a moment of hope for everyone, and we were all holding back tears. When we finished, she tried to speak to me more politely, and I explained that I hadn't understood why she was accusing me of speaking rudely to her. I understood perfectly about the time; she saw I was about to burst into tears and advised me that it wasn't good to react like that in my condition. I think such considerations should be made from the very beginning. Afterward, I felt very sad for not having enjoyed the moment after waiting so long for it. I'm really sorry because the woman who attended to me the first time was wonderful, but we won't be going back.

My experience with Clínica Dorsia has been appalling. I'm due for my annual check-up, and I've been going from clinic to clinic for ages trying to get an appointment with Dr. Magide. It's outrageous to have to chase after clinics to get an appointment for a check-up that's rightfully mine.

After being sent from one place to another, when I finally try to resolve the issue, I'm told that the doctor is only available for two hours one day and that I have to keep calling because his schedule isn't open yet. In other words, I have to keep calling, again and again, without anyone giving me a concrete solution or guaranteeing when I'll be able to have my check-up.

Is this really the kind of care a patient deserves after undergoing treatment at your clinic? I don't think it's the patient's responsibility to be constantly calling to get an appointment, or to waste time chasing after an appointment that should be managed in an organized way.

The impression you give is one of complete disorganization and a lack of consideration for the people who trust you. Booking and undergoing treatment seems much simpler, but when it comes to check-ups and follow-up appointments, the runaround, excuses, and endless waits begin.

I'm not asking for any favors. I'm demanding a follow-up appointment that I'm overdue and a clear solution, not being told to keep calling without knowing when I'll be seen.

My dissatisfaction is immense, and frankly, the experience has been disappointing. I wouldn't recommend Clínica Dorsia based on the treatment I'm receiving. I hope they take post-operative care seriously, organize appointments better, and stop stringing along patients who simply want the follow-up care they're entitled to, since they've paid for it.

I'm giving it one star because I can't give it less, and I hope they don't delete the review so people don't see how inept they are.

THEY ARE SCAMMERS!! IN CAPITAL LETTERS!!!

My mother had emergency surgery at Christmas and couldn't have it done with them. This was all advised by a woman named Silvia, who deceived her as much as possible. They've been giving her the runaround about returning her money, and she still hasn't gotten it back. She's paying off a loan they gave her, which she can't even use because the surgeon himself told her she's not eligible due to the surgery she had.

To this day, we still haven't received any answers because every time we go, they change the manager, and every time we go, they tell us something different.

Beware of deposits. My wife went to ask for a quote for breast augmentation surgery, and they made it sound easy: they assured us that if we left a €100 deposit, it would be refunded without any problem if she ultimately decided not to have the surgery. She decided against it, requested a refund, and now they're refusing to give her the money back, citing excuses they never mentioned at the beginning. Zero transparency and not a word from them. I don't recommend them.

Scammers, I absolutely do not recommend this place. The service is terrible. You pay for a treatment, and if it doesn't turn out well, they inject the entire vial, and if there are any flaws, they don't fix anything. They leave you exactly as you were. If you want to correct something, they tell you to pay for a new vial to fix it, and you have to put up with it. The directors keep giving you the runaround, each one worse than the last, saying there's no solution and that if you want to fix it, you have to pay for another vial. So, I left. I asked for a complaint form, and that's it. I will never return to this clinic. The Botox and hyaluronic acid treatment was a complete waste after a month, and it didn't show any results at all. My money was thrown in the trash.

I am very angry and disappointed with the treatment I received. While you're considering the treatment, everything is easy, friendly, and full of kind words, but once you've paid, the situation changes completely. It was only after they charged me that they told me the product is injected all at once and that there are no subsequent touch-ups. I find it shameful that such important information isn't clearly explained before the client pays.

The worst part is the feeling that once they have your money, if you don't like the result, it's your problem. What if you're not satisfied with the result? What if you were expecting something different? The answer I received was, in practice, that there's no solution and you have to accept it.

I feel cheated because that information would have influenced my decision. It's not just about the money, but about the lack of transparency and the little consideration for the patient. When someone undergoes cosmetic treatment, they are placing their trust in the professionals, and that trust is broken when such important aspects are communicated at the last minute.

I do not recommend this clinic. I wish I had read experiences like this before going, because it would have saved me a lot of money, distress, and frustration. The worst part is that after stringing me along for several weeks, they laughed in my face and told me they weren't going to fix anything, just like that. So, complaint form. I'll never go back in my life. What a scam of a clinic! And the director at the Pedro Antonio clinic is terrible; the service is awful.

one_star_reviews.text: If you have fibromyalgia or back injuries, don't waste your money. I bought a €315 voucher for two of the three services they offer: cryotherapy (four sessions) and six sessions of the waist trainer for belly reduction. I told them from the start that I have fibromyalgia and bad knees, and the woman told me everything would be great for me. The explanations were quite vague, with little explanation of the process itself and a lot of explanation of biology. In short: the cryotherapy involved spending a few minutes in temperatures almost -200 degrees Celsius, and the waist trainer was supposed to keep your heart rate up for an hour, supposedly resulting in a loss of up to 8 cm. Following her instructions, I went on the first day with some weights, resistance bands, and a few other things to maintain the indicated heart rate for an hour. To my surprise, you have to spend an hour on a stationary bike—one of those with a tiny seat and a hunched position. After 10 minutes, my whole body ached. I mentioned to Maria that for people with back pain or fibromyalgia, they could use one of those bikes with a backrest and a regular seat for comfort. Her response was, "These cheap bikes do the job, but if you can't even last 10 minutes on a bike, you're not going to achieve anything." If I'd known I'd have to do an hour-long bike ride, I would have signed up. I didn't lose anything in terms of my waist; instead, I ended up with back, shoulder, and neck pain that lasted two months. In certain areas, I even had to bring a cushion to sit on. I also developed knee pain on top of what I already had, and I had to pay for physical therapy for two months. My orthopedist asked me how I'd even thought of it... that cycling is good, but only with machines adapted to the needs of people with back pain. As for the cold, my metabolism might have noticed something... I didn't feel a thing. Sometimes it's better not to try for "miracles."

Neither Druni nor their shipping company, Tipsa, have the slightest consideration for their customers.
More than three weeks ago, I placed an order and was told it would arrive within 48-72 hours at the most. They sent me an email saying it would arrive the next day.
When I saw that my package hadn't arrived, I contacted both Druni and Tipsa, but neither offered a solution; they just kept passing the buck.
Druni's main office told me to wait a few days, that they would call Tipsa and then call me back. Ten more days have passed, and they haven't called, so I called again, and they told me the same thing: they have to call Tipsa to find out what happened to the package.

I requested a refund, exercising my legal right to claim my money within 14 days, and they told me they couldn't refund me before knowing the package's location and condition.
Look, that's their responsibility, not mine. They can refund my money and make all the calls they deem necessary, but I'm not going to lose my money because some call center agents can't manage their own logistics properly. They haven't the faintest idea, neither the operators who answer the phone at Druni nor Tipsa.
The result is that my package is lost, and since Druni, according to them, has to call Tipsa (which they've been trying to do for over two weeks now, and apparently they don't have the time), my money was lost along with my order. They were quick enough to charge me, as I hadn't even placed the order yet. That's the speed I want now so I can get my money back, but these liars and swindlers keep pulling the wool over my eyes, saying they have to call... Well, they should call on the first day and actually serve the customers.

I feel ripped off by both Druni and Tipsa. Neither of them is offering a solution, and they're just busy blaming each other, saying neither is to blame. But I'm the one who's not to blame.

In short, be careful with these companies, especially Druni, because they don't have the right staff, and those staff members lack the minimum professional and interpersonal skills to deal with customers.
DRUNI, A TERRIBLE COMPANY.
ALERT WAY!!!

one_star_reviews.text:
Writing
A Disappointing Experience
About a year ago, I went to Decorlyt in Ibi for advice on how to maintain the water in my above-ground pool during the winter. They confidently recommended using a specific product to preserve the water during that period.
I followed their advice, and when I removed the cover this summer, I found that the pool had lost a considerable amount of color and, more worryingly, the cover had weakened.
I feel it's important to share my experience because I went to a specialized store specifically seeking advice and trusting their recommendation. I expected the product to be suitable for an above-ground pool and to remain in contact with the cover for months.
I believe that when a product is recommended with such certainty, the type of pool and the material of the cover should be carefully considered, and any potential risks should be clearly warned against.
Based on my experience, I am disappointed with the advice I received and believe they should review these types of recommendations.

Regarding the last review on Google under the name Jesús, and in response to the establishment, I want to clarify that it was at the store located on Paseo de Rollo, and yes, there was indeed a dispute. They told me that "you can't enter the bank knowing the closing time, even if it's open," and that "they had enough to eat even if they lost a customer."

It's also worth noting that they refused to process the card payment for the customer in front of me, claiming "the card reader was off." This is all quite surprising because, as I said, there were still 15 minutes until closing time. It would have been much easier, and above all, there wouldn't have been any problem, if they had informed me upon entering that they wouldn't be able to serve me. However, I was not informed of this at any point before placing my order.

We are regular customers of Hermanos Martín, and the service has always been exceptional in all their stores, which is why this situation is so concerning, and I want to make it known.

I believe that when working with the public, courtesy, professionalism, and a friendly approach should always be paramount. Product quality is important, but customer service is what truly makes the difference and determines whether someone wants to return or not. Good service and respectful treatment should be essential in any business.

one_star_reviews.text:
I'm very unhappy. Specifically, Rocío, a know-it-all woman. She's more out there than a subway. Here's my situation: I ordered 7 pallets of concrete blocks, 30 bags of cement, and 2 sacks of gravel. Delivery was separate, costing €96. So far, so good.

The morning they were supposed to deliver it, a week after I'd visited the warehouse, this woman called me asking if there was any way I could pick up the two sacks. I told her no, that if I could, I wouldn't be paying for delivery. She said they wouldn't fit in the truck and that she'd have to charge me for another delivery. "That's your logistics problem," I replied. "I already paid for the delivery; you figure it out." In the end, she gave in and they delivered it. The worst part is that once the delivery arrived—the driver, Raúl, is an excellent person—I paid him because the amount matched the quote I'd received from the warehouse and the goods were correct. The problem is that when I check the invoices, I see they've charged me for 7 pallets at €15 plus VAT each. That's a total of €127.50, which I didn't order, which they didn't tell me were included, and which, as always, the carrier (in this case, the warehouse) is responsible for collecting because they own the pallets. It's the warehouse's responsibility to come and pick them up, since they're theirs, and they've decided to avoid the trip and make me pay €127.
I've requested a refund so they can come and collect their pallets whenever they want. If they don't refund the money, they've been warned I'll file a complaint with the consumer protection agency. I don't recommend this warehouse.

It's a disgrace; we've been cruelly deceived. We're going to request an inspection from the Community of Madrid.
We've gone to the authorities to report our ordeal at the care home.
We'll proceed according to the advice they've given us.
Yesterday, September 3rd of this year, we admitted my mother after she was discharged from the hospital following surgery.
After six interminable hours of interviews and signing the contract and internal regulations that aren't being followed, they showed us the shared room they'd assigned her.
It smelled bad, there were bags full of who-knows-what all over the room, her roommate had an ashtray with cigarettes on the terrace, food on the table, shoes on the floor... so the living conditions of that so-called room were nonexistent, especially in the case of an 85-year-old woman with heart disease who had recently undergone cancer surgery.
This is a blatant rip-off that cannot be tolerated.
Don't trust their empty promises; inside the care home, there's absolutely no control over the residents or their actions. We will seek compensation for damages, as we have all suffered greatly after this incident; they have played with the feelings of a very elderly person who needs care and attention.

one_star_reviews.text:
ABSOLUTELY DISGRACEFUL SERVICE. AVOID THIS PHARMACY.

On 24 August 2026, I went to this pharmacy because my father had developed a severe dental abscess while we were on holiday. We were carrying an emergency antibiotic, and I simply asked for professional advice on whether he should take it or seek medical attention. The man who assisted me showed no empathy whatsoever and dismissed us rudely with: “Go and see a doctor.”

We followed that advice and went to a nearby dental clinic, only to be told that they had no appointments available for three months. I therefore contacted my dentist in Portugal for urgent help. He quickly assessed the situation, prescribed amoxicillin, and sent me an official electronic prescription issued by the Portuguese National Health Service. He explained that the medication should be available from a pharmacy in Spain, as both countries are members of the EU.

When I returned to this pharmacy with a valid medical prescription, a woman claimed that they could not read its QR code and insisted that I find a doctor in Spain, pay for another appointment, and obtain a Spanish prescription. Even worse, she mocked the situation by saying: “Yes, we are all part of the EU, but you cannot use this prescription in Spain.”

Her attitude was arrogant, sarcastic, obstructive, and completely devoid of compassion for a patient suffering from a serious dental condition.

My Portuguese dentist considered the situation absurd and raised the possibility that the pharmacy either had an interest in directing patients to the clinic it recommended or did not want to dispense medication prescribed through the Portuguese National Health Service.

We then went to another nearby pharmacy. They accepted EXACTLY THE SAME PRESCRIPTION and handed me the antibiotic within TWO MINUTES. No drama, no sarcasm and no attempt to send us elsewhere.

This proves that the problem was not the prescription—it was this pharmacy and its appalling attitude.

Being conveniently located near the beach does not excuse this level of rudeness, arrogance and lack of professionalism. When someone is seeking urgent help for a painful medical condition, the very least they deserve is respectful and compassionate treatment.

One of the worst pharmacy experiences I have ever had. PLEASE GO SOMEWHERE ELSE.

My boyfriend and I went to the piercing studio today at 5:30 PM because of the promotion. I wanted to get dermal piercings on my back, so I went to the studio alone with the piercer. She didn't warn me that she was going to pierce me. I asked her another question, and she answered rudely. I decided to leave before she finished putting the jewelry in. I left crying, not because of the pain of the piercing, but because you go to a piercing studio and try to establish some kind of relationship with the professional to feel more comfortable and less afraid. The service was terrible. I already have several piercings, and this is the first time I've had such a grotesque experience.

The first time I let it slide because I thought it was my fault for not being able to express myself, but now I realize it's them. I'm never going back.

one_star_reviews.text:
The worst private health insurance company by far. And I've experienced it twice.
For years I paid the maximum premium, and when you need them, they cover nothing. They don't always have specialists available. The service is very precarious and sporadically inadequate. My father needed them after a lifetime of paying into the company, and when he got cancer, they abandoned him.
They referred me to the General Hospital of Catalonia because they didn't have emergency specialists, and when they were going to do the neurology tests, they told me no and to go back to them (the private health insurance company). An inhumane mess.
My review is clear: IF YOU DON'T WANT TO BE CHEATED AND LEFT STRANDED, DON'T JOIN THIS INSURANCE COMPANY.

At the Granollers health insurance clinic, the service is terrible in many departments. In the last one I visited recently, the assistant was completely out of it, chattering away and ignoring the phone, which kept ringing in the waiting room. Even the doctor mentioned it. The doctor was very nice, but the assistant, with her airs of superiority, completely ignored her. The patients in the waiting room questioned her behavior. It's a disgrace. The waiting lists in some departments are shameful, and the restrooms... they could really use a facelift. I'm glad I cancelled my membership, like so many others, because it's not what it used to be. The service is a zero. I'm forced to give it one star, but it doesn't deserve any.

one_star_reviews.text:
Absolutely disappointing, Gabriela.
I absolutely do not recommend her.

My partner and I went to therapy seeking tools to address our problems, especially communication issues. However, when the idea of ​​accepting each other as we are was raised, I felt the approach didn't align with what we were looking for. If a couple seeks therapy specifically to work on certain behaviors and dynamics, I believe there should be a space to address and work on them, not simply accept them as something to be accepted.

For this reason, I decided not to continue with the sessions. She then continued seeing my partner individually, which I consider inappropriate and, in my opinion, could conflict with certain basic principles of the professional code of ethics, given that she had previously worked with both partners.

In short, a year later, my assessment is profoundly negative. I believe the process did not help our relationship, as it ultimately ended.

If you are a couple and are looking for professional help, I recommend that you thoroughly research the professional's approach and, especially, verify their training and registration before starting a therapeutic process.

one_star_reviews.text:
My experience with Fertilab was unfortunately not a positive one. Throughout the entire process, we were mainly supported through a third person, while Dr. Ana Belén Casas, who was supposed to be the doctor following our case, only spoke with us during two video consultations.

The second consultation took place after our treatment had failed, and it was particularly difficult for me. The doctor, in a manner that I found cold, lacking in empathy and extremely blunt, told us that in most cases when a treatment fails in this way, the cause lies with the woman and the quality of her eggs. According to her, I should undergo another stimulation with a stronger protocol and, if that also failed, consider egg donation.

After that conversation, I cried for days. What makes me even more upset today is that my situation was not nearly as hopeless as it had been presented to me. We changed clinics and underwent another stimulation in Italy, not simply with a “stronger” treatment, but with a different protocol that was better suited to me. The outcome was completely different: 15 eggs retrieved, 6 blastocysts and 4 euploid embryos. Today, I am pregnant after our first embryo transfer.

I fully understand that no fertility clinic can guarantee the success of IVF. What I object to is the ease and coldness with which, so soon after a failed treatment, I was told something so devastating and was already presented with egg donation as the next option, without first properly exploring the possibility that the protocol simply might not have been the right one for me.

This experience also taught me that sometimes you don’t need to travel so far to find excellent specialists. They may be much closer to home than you think.

one_star_reviews.text:
​As returning customers who have rented canoes here for the past three years, we were extremely disappointed by the complete lack of organization and disrespect for our time.
​We booked full-day canoes online for a group of 10 people and paid the entire amount in advance. After driving two hours from Madrid, we arrived at 11:30 AM only to be told they had no boats left because the morning shift hadn't returned—which makes no sense given we had booked a full-day rental. They redirected us to a partner location 3 minutes away.
​We were patient, drove over, got changed, and were ready to enter the river when they dropped another bomb: there were no boats there either. Their solution was simply to offer a full refund.
​A refund does not fix a wasted four-hour round trip, lost gas, and a ruined day for 10 people. Overselling bookings and wasting customers' time like this is completely unacceptable. We will not be coming back.
