one_star_reviews.text: Terrible service and appalling customer service. I arrived at the gas station around 7:30 pm and asked the woman there for 15 euros worth of diesel. To begin with, the woman serving me made a mistake and put 5 euros worth of gasoline in my tank, until I told her to stop because she wasn't putting diesel in. Then she told me it was fine and that if I filled the tank with diesel, nothing would happen to the car, but I replied that I couldn't fill the tank for my own reasons (since I'm a student and work at the same time) and until I get paid, I can't afford it, so I started looking for other options to resolve the situation. While I was looking, the woman (a rude woman) started muttering in the background that if I didn't have money for gasoline, I shouldn't buy a car and that "people these days don't think things through." While she was saying this, she also came closer to me and told me to find a solution myself, like asking someone for money or taking out a loan, because she wasn't going to call Repsol's insurance company to have the tank emptied for 3 liters of gasoline, and she wasn't going to pay for the diesel either (all the while telling me things about her life to try and teach me a lesson, as if I were the one who had made the mistake instead of her). At one point, since she'd been saying these awful things to me for a while, I told her that I was obviously a student and couldn't afford it, and she did nothing better than threaten me, saying, "Well, I'd better not see you drinking a €10 drink in the street," among other things. In the end, I had to sort everything out myself, asking my mother for money, since we don't have money to spare, to solve a problem that we didn't even cause because she "wasn't going to call the insurance company for something so trivial."

Run away from this woman.

one_star_reviews.text:
If you're going to see a psychiatrist through your private health insurance company for sick leave, you'd better prepare yourself because no matter what you do, no matter how many documents you present from professionals (who didn't even read them, by the way), and no matter what you say, they'll discharge you because that's what the insurance company dictates. It seems like they're paid or get a commission for issuing discharges, just like that.

In my case, I went twice and saw two different psychiatrists, Dr. Miguel Wenceslao De Andrés Mosquera and Dr. Pablo Garcés Ballesteros. A 10-minute interview where I felt judged and unheard, and to top it all off, at the end of the session, they give you a tablet where you have to answer all the questions. I consider this an archaic methodology that assesses other mental disorders bordering on dementia.

Finally, I want to emphasize that the report they submit to the insurance company will always state you are fit to work. They won't mention any of the symptoms you described in the interview, and they'll even fabricate details such as the session duration (always stating it was longer than you were actually there), twist your words, and, to top it all off, include spelling mistakes and errors in the patient's information. This demonstrates their lack of professionalism and the rush they must be under.

Naturally, after some time, I received the medical discharge proposed by the insurance company doctor based solely on the report prepared by these so-called "psychiatrists." I appealed this discharge to the ICAM (Catalan Institute of Medical Assessments) in Tarragona, and they denied it simply because of the report submitted by these individuals.

Abysmal service and a disgrace to the professionals they claim to be. I hope this review joins the many others who have gone through the same thing and serves as a warning to those who will go in the future, so they know what to expect.

one_star_reviews.text:
I DO NOT RECOMMEND THIS CLINIC. It has been very disappointing. I had a gastric balloon inserted hoping for serious treatment and professional follow-up, but in my case, it was absolutely useless. I feel like I wasted my money.

The nutritional follow-up provided by the nutritionist Laura was very poor. The person who treated me as a "nutritionist" didn't inspire any confidence or demonstrate the knowledge I expected to help me change my habits or answer my questions. Instead of feeling supported, I felt completely alone throughout the process. They completely ignore you once you pay, and on top of having to travel to another city, they don't even reimburse you for travel expenses despite the considerable sum you invest. When I had complications, my experience was that they told me to go to the emergency room in my city, and I felt I didn't receive the follow-up I expected from the clinic.

Regarding the psychological support, it was also a huge disappointment. They laugh at you. Every day they changed psychologists, and none of them left much to be desired. It's sold as an important part of the treatment, but in my experience, the sessions offered absolutely nothing. I didn't receive the professional support I needed to face this kind of change.

In short, my experience has been very negative. I invested a significant amount of money, 4,000 euros. I understand that each patient can have a different experience, but this has been mine. Personally, I don't recommend it. I would not recommend this clinic because I feel that the care I received was not up to the standard I expected, nor was it commensurate with the financial investment made.

To my surprise, she rudely told me she could only refund the bikini top because the bottoms were stained with a non-existent white mark. Not satisfied, she rudely threw the bottoms on the counter and arrogantly repeated the statement, adding that they make sure the clothes leave the store clean. I told her again that there was no stain, and she rudely showed me the "invisible stain" again. In short, degrading treatment, poor manners, and arrogance. Don't waste your money and time in these kinds of stores with these kinds of employees. I work in customer service, and it never in my life has crossed my mind to speak to a customer the way this girl spoke to me. Unfortunately, I didn't catch her name, but she's probably the manager because she's wearing a white shirt, unlike the rest of the employees who are wearing black ones.

one_star_reviews.text: Well, after two years of my daughter attending the center, and after indicating that we would be on vacation for two weeks during September, imagine my surprise when they charged me the full monthly fee. When I told them it was a mistake, they said it wasn't, that it was correct, and that it was company policy, and that they even require a signature. If they are on vacation, they don't charge you, but if you go outside of the summer break (September), they charge you no matter what, due to their organization. If you want to change a class, which is impossible, they call you to change it for you, and you do them a favor so they can fill the gaps! Well, I'm not going to be taken for a ride anymore! Very bad, very bad indeed! The problem is that you're full, but I hope people choose other centers where they don't deceive them! You only get paid if you do the work, not if you haven't taught the class and you were given a month's notice. Because, of course, in August you weren't bothered because you were on vacation and couldn't organize groups! THAT'S NOT HOW THINGS WORK!!

one_star_reviews.text:
I signed up a few years ago, so I can offer an objective opinion.

During the interview, I clearly explained my personality and preferences, especially my age and lifestyle.

I was undecided between this place and another, but I thought that with the TV advertising LAZOS was getting, I'd have a better chance here. But I was wrong.

It's not just the difficulty they have finding suitable people to make introductions, but also their lack of flexibility, imagination, and enthusiasm for their work.

In my case, my first introduction was disastrous; we didn't even meet in person. I can understand this when someone idealizes a person's image based on photos (which is why I'm against showing photos on first dates, and for this first introduction, I wanted to trust them and sent photos).

The second was even worse. They wanted to introduce me to a man who was older than the age I had initially stated. I agreed out of obligation, but it was quite humiliating. And when I saw him in person, he scared me even more.

The third one was a really nice guy, but he didn't fit at all with what I told him I was looking for... however, as a friend he seemed really nice, but not for the purpose for which I signed up with Lazos...

The fourth one, I didn't even bother trying... I was already burned out... and I didn't want to see his pictures either, so I wouldn't be scared by an image that doesn't even correspond to reality. I completely lost interest.

The fifth and last one I remember, he was in a huge rush, which is exactly what I don't want in my life: to be pressured... we were barely talking, and what little we did talk about was already about his rush to start a family... and what about me? That guy didn't want a girl to fall in love with, he wanted to have kids... How do you expect me to get to know someone like that? Especially after seeing everything I'd been introduced to before... and to top it all off, the "guy," if you can even call him that, spoke badly about me.

She never contacted me again, and honestly, given the lack of originality in introducing me to people, with so few options for how we present ourselves and so little effort put into making it look good, it's probably for the best...

As for my physical appearance, like everyone else, some people will like it and some won't... in fact, in my experience, I can say that I'm usually liked... I'm not a top model, especially not in photos, but even people I've met online who later saw me in person couldn't believe I was the person they were talking to behind the screen... I don't see myself as all that, but people are surprised when they see me in person, because, personally, photos don't do me any favors.

Anyway, disappointment doesn't even begin to cover it... INNOVATION is definitely not the word that defines LAZOS...

It's a frustrating, months-long waiting game.

It's a SHAME to have to spend months chasing these people. Neither I nor anyone in my circle will go near this store again, and I hope those who read the reviews won't either.
To top it all off, you respond to reviews asking us to index the number of requests made on your website when you know perfectly well who we are, the problem we have, and that it can't be discussed here.

I will continue to update my review, contact the Consumer Protection Agency, and ultimately, I will take more drastic legal action.

By the way, Esther is very friendly when you book (too friendly, in fact), but if you want a refund: forget it. She doesn't even answer.

If you call the clinic to schedule an appointment with the address: they never give you one, nor do they return your call.

FIRST REVIEW:
My experience with Dorsia Cartagena has been very disappointing. I requested a refund in April for a treatment that wasn't fully completed, and to this day, I'm still waiting for a solution. During these months (6 months, to be exact), I've received numerous responses indicating that "it's approved" or that "they will contact me," but without providing me with the refund amount, a breakdown of the calculation, or the documentation I've requested repeatedly. Of course, they still haven't issued the refund.

one_star_reviews.text:
Dissatisfied
I had melasma treatment with Dr. Juanes and didn't see a single change in my skin. The doctor insisted there was a change, but I see it as the same or worse. I'm very dissatisfied. It's supposed to be one of the best clinics.

Unfortunately, I had a very bad experience. I'm a long-time customer and I booked an appointment to discuss my daughter's acne. They gave me an appointment for 8:00 PM on a weekday. The first bad experience was at reception. The person who attended to us wasn't particularly friendly, but above all, she didn't enunciate at all and spoke listlessly. My daughter and I had to ask her several times to repeat herself. Second, it seemed like she was having trouble with the appointment in the system; she had to ask a colleague for help. That wasn't particularly bad, but what came next was. We went up to the fourth floor and waited. Since there was no one to speak to on the fourth floor, after half an hour in the waiting room, I went back down to reception to ask what was happening with our appointment. The very pleasant young woman from the beginning told me that the system showed we had already been seen, and even that my daughter had received treatment. The doctor who was going to see her had just left. Overall, a very bad experience. It's understandable that there might be a problem in an isolated case, but the receptionist lacked the empathy to convey how sorry she was or how she could help. All she could think to say was that this was very rare and never happened... PS: I recommend the center be more careful in selecting doctors for cosmetic treatments. The doctor who was supposed to treat us, and whom we saw leave before even seeing us, had clearly undergone several cosmetic procedures herself, which were very visible and unnatural. This makes me not want to return for my daughter's treatment. She doesn't inspire much confidence. I'm very saddened by this experience because I have fond memories of being a laser patient there many years ago.

I'm posting this review to warn future patients before they make a decision with Dr. Alba Martínez. My sister underwent surgery with her, and the experience was disastrous, both in terms of the medical results and the management and post-operative follow-up.

We encountered a complete lack of professionalism, little empathy for the complications that arose, and care that left much to be desired during a critical moment. A procedure that should have been safe turned into an ordeal filled with negligence and anguish. I strongly recommend seeking second opinions and completely avoiding her so that you don't go through the same thing.

one_star_reviews.text:
I was here from around 2016 to early 2018. The only thing I remember is that the psychologist (Ana) would sometimes laugh at me, constantly interrupt me, and try to control my life, suppressing my desire to read or study philosophy. I listened to her, but I ended up suppressing my own personality, believing that if I followed her "advice" I would get better, but it was quite the opposite. She made unprofessional comments, for example, saying things like, "Why is it that people with mental disorders like philosophy and poetry?" (Saying this while looking at the ceiling), she lacked empathy, didn't respect my tastes, labeled me with many comments but very few positive ones. I had to endure bullying in a vocational training course in organic farming in El Prat, but she didn't care, she didn't provide any resources or support for me to deal with it (even though I was brutally bullied in primary and secondary school). On top of that, she once told me: "Character is having the capacity to overcome traumas and well, you..." (referring to the fact that I had no character or personality). I even attempted suicide, and she called it a "very immature action." Imagine how I felt when I heard that. The last thing she said to me was: "Come back whenever you want," after I was fired from my first job. A horrible and disastrous experience; I wasted a lot of money on her. Now, luckily, I'm being treated at the Cornellá Mental Health Center by a decent psychiatrist and another private psychologist who understands me and doesn't do silly or stupid things like Ana.

Edit: What a surprise that after My negative experience and review explaining what I went through with Ana are filled with positive reviews saying what a good professional she is... I was a patient who tried hard, I had depression with suicidal tendencies, but Ana didn't care at all.

one_star_reviews.text:
My Experience with This Dental Clinic
After almost four years of orthodontic treatment, my experience has been completely disappointing. Now, I find myself having to start a new orthodontic treatment at another clinic, including the need for micro-screws, which means more time, more discomfort, and additional expense. Throughout this time, I have attended my appointments regularly, and in my experience, the radiographic follow-up has been insufficient: in approximately four years of treatment, I have only had one x-ray, despite wearing braces the entire time.

Furthermore, during the treatment, I have had dental problems that particularly concern me. Tooth #16, which had already been restored, fractured and developed cavities again, and I currently also have a cavity in tooth #17. I have also experienced gum problems and inflammation.

What worries me most is that now, when I go to another clinic to assess my situation, they tell me I need another orthodontic treatment with micro-screws to try to correct the problem.

After so many years, I believe that someone starting orthodontic treatment places their trust in the professional, expecting proper follow-up and controlled progress. In my case, I feel I've wasted time and money and now I practically have to start all over again.

I'm sharing my experience so that others are well-informed before deciding where to get orthodontic treatment. I recommend always requesting copies of x-rays, reports, and complete treatment documentation, and seeking a second opinion if something isn't progressing as it should.
My intention isn't to harm anyone, but rather to publicly share what happened to me and prevent someone else from finding themselves in a similar situation.

Lack of commitment and professionalism. You have absolutely no empathy for the people whose time you waste. Kesia is terrible at diagnosing.
I went to have the acid removed, and after months of being given the runaround and being left hanging, they told me the only solution was to pay another €300, in a very rude manner and without any guarantee of getting the result I wanted or expected.
If Kesia is the one who assesses you on the first day, she should be accompanied by the doctor who will be treating you later, and both opinions should be similar, because otherwise, you waste time and money and end up disappointed.

My experience at this clinic was very negative. I went to have the hyaluronic acid removed from my lips using hyaluronidase. Before the appointment, they charged me for the syringe, and on several occasions, different people at the clinic assured me that they had the product.

When I arrived on the day of my appointment, they informed me that the hyaluronidase was out of stock and, as an alternative, offered to inject me with a toxin used for other treatments, which was neither what I had requested nor what I had paid for.

The worst part was the way I was treated: instead of offering a solution, an apology, or a refund for a product they didn't have, they simply told me they couldn't do anything.

I consider this a serious lack of professionalism, especially for a cosmetic procedure where I believe it's essential to know exactly what product will be used. I left there with a great deal of distrust and very disappointed with the management and, above all, with the treatment I received from Kesia.

I don't understand why Kesia is your "advisor" or what criteria she uses for her diagnosis, if it doesn't agree at all with the doctor's assessment in the office. Besides not letting anyone speak, she tries to outdo you and contradicts everything you say, leaving you frustrated and bitter—all after you've already paid for treatment.
They don't solve anything when you have a "problem" that they themselves created, due to their roles or hierarchy in the practice. There are so many advisors and so many people wandering around those halls, and all they do is waste your time and money. They don't care in the slightest how you are or how you feel, and I believe that nowadays, everyone's time is equally valuable.
You are incompetent. You don't even bother to call your patients to offer any solution other than making them spend more money to fix the mess you make. Four months behind you, and after being there talking, he turns around and leaves with the word in his mouth, telling you that it's his time and that he's leaving.

If I could, I'd give you -200 stars.

If you're planning on getting treatment with them, make sure the doctor assesses you from day one because Kesia is all about sales, painting everything as perfect and then washing her hands of it. She has zero interest in anything but making a sale. A terrible experience.

I entered the shop with my two daughters, aged four and ten. They were checking a toy. The eldest daughter removed a sticker from the toy to demonstrate its workings to her younger sister. She then placed it back the toy with  the sticker . Suddenly, a seller approached her rudely, demanding payment and accusing her of miss using the toys . I was just three steps  away, getting some sunscreen, and returned to pay when I found my daughter crying.

Firstly, let’s consider the context. This is a shop in the airport where children come to see, and maybe if something gets their attention to buy  a  toy. She didn’t break anything; she didn’t remove it from a package, she did not brake it and she wasn’t alone for more than five minutes. Couldn’t the seller have waited a moment and approached me to explain what was happening? Instead, it was easier to come and make a child cry and accuse me of not educating my daughter properly. Seriously?  Please lady  change jobs because we’re customers with children in the airport’s kids’ section, and they didn’t exhibit inappropriate behaviour.

Please avoid coming to the duty-free shop, El Merecido. Give your money to someone else.

To the lady who intervened and said nothing happened:

Yes, nothing happened. I agree that nothing happened that I couldn’t have apologised for, paid for the toy, or adhered to the shop’s policy. But why did it happen? What happened is a bad experience and unnecessary use of power from an adult to a children…

To the male manager or colleague that talked to my daughter and tried to calm her …. thanks for your attention to us and kindness….

one_star_reviews.text: Terrible experience and unacceptable treatment of a 71-year-old man after a stroke. Attention and care were completely lacking. The resident fell asleep three days after arriving and spent a considerable amount of time lying on the floor. Now he has another CT scan due to a fall. What kind of resident management do you have? He contracted a virus within the center, where several others were infected. We were notified in advance to test and isolate those who were infected, but management took no action whatsoever and failed to conduct any follow-up tests. Their response to my emails was an excuse that they weren't responsible for testing or providing a proper wheelchair (which didn't even have a footrest), telling him to buy one himself. Shameful responses! You should have the appropriate equipment and be preventing infections, not putting all the elderly residents and their lives, as well as their visitors and caregivers, at risk. He's now at home with a positive virus and has lung problems. He was going here for rehabilitation, and not once was he allowed to sit in a chair from morning till night. They don't even check if he's eating, and he's been eating only pureed food for 20 days straight. Then they put him on the same diet. The weekly menu is pathetic, the worst place imaginable. Don't even take your worst enemy there. It's the worst management and lack of humanity I've ever seen. I absolutely do not recommend this place. Of course, legal action will be taken with all the evidence so they don't do this to anyone else or claim the accusations are false. They abuse vulnerable and sick people, laugh in everyone's face, endanger the health of others, and send people home without checking for the virus, even though it was required that they be tested before leaving. They don't even do that. It's been 20 days of repeating the same thing, ignoring all the complaints with medical reports, photos, and emails that justify it. If you're not fit to run a care home properly or care for the elderly, then get another job. You certainly earn a good salary, and you're quick to sign contracts without even reading them to the residents... I hope social services and the inspection service take action on all of this. Your accusations are completely unfounded. People go to the care home to improve things and come back worse than when they arrived, with RSV+ virus. Besides sending them home without showering, without washing their clothes, and without eating on the day of their voluntary discharge due to dissatisfaction with the care, you should be ashamed. I hope care homes like this are shut down because nobody deserves this treatment, much less having their health jeopardized—those of us who actually care for them and look after their well-being.

one_star_reviews.text:
I had a ticket for August 25th from Ibiza to Mallorca and arrived at the port with 25 minutes before departure. Staff refused to let me through security, citing I had to be there 1 hour prior to departure, which is not factual as online it says you have to be there 15 minutes prior if you’re traveling without a car. When I asked the employee handling boarding for their name, I was told they couldn’t provide it due to “company policy.”

I filed a formal complaint (hoja de reclamación) on-site. one_star_reviews.text:
⭐ 1/5 — An Absolutely Catastrophic Service

On Monday, August 24, I went with my family to Ceuta’s Maritime Park. After spending some time at the swimming pool, we were hungry and noticed that there were several pizzerias inside the park, including Telepizza and Domino’s Pizza.

Telepizza was packed, while Domino’s was practically empty. We couldn’t understand why, especially since it was Monday and Domino’s had a promotion. Despite this, almost everyone was at Telepizza. I should clearly have taken the hint and gone elsewhere.

I decided to try Domino’s anyway… and it was a huge mistake.

There were only two employees running the restaurant: one in the kitchen and the other responsible for taking orders and serving customers. However, instead of properly focusing on his work, we saw the latter taking orders with one hand in his pocket and the other on his phone, looking at his screen while dealing with customers. This immediately gave us an idea of the level of professionalism and organization at the restaurant.

We ordered two pizzas and some nuggets. As a result, we waited almost an hour before receiving our pizzas. The worst part was that I eventually had to go and get them myself. They had been ready for more than 20 minutes and were simply sitting on the counter, without anyone bothering to bring them to our table.

The nuggets were even worse: we had to wait an additional 30 minutes.

At one point, the employee came to our table with a plate of nuggets and called another customer’s name. We therefore told him that it wasn’t our order. He went back with the plate and simply left it somewhere else. In the end, we discovered that the plate was actually… our order.

When we pointed out that this level of service was completely unacceptable, instead of apologizing or trying to find a solution, one of the employees replied rudely: “If you’re not happy, go to Telepizza.” That is exactly what we ended up doing for our children.

Catastrophic service, nonexistent organization, an interminable wait, and a completely inappropriate attitude toward customers.

Having known Domino’s Pizza for some time, I intend to forward this review to the company and ask a manager to investigate how this restaurant is being run, particularly to determine whether it is a franchise. If so, this restaurant is truly bringing shame on the brand and seriously damaging its reputation.

I now completely understand why Domino’s was empty while Telepizza was packed.

One thing is certain: I will never set foot in this restaurant again. For a brand like Domino’s, this level of service is simply unacceptable.

Go to telepizza !

one_star_reviews.text:
I'm going to change my review... let me explain. A few years ago, my wife and I went to couples therapy. I didn't connect with her in the first session, but I did in the second, third, fourth, and fifth. It helped us quite a bit, but I think that more than the psychologist's professionalism, what helped us (or at least me) was listening to and being listened to by my partner and someone neutral. After having several sessions as a couple, we also had some individual sessions. Today, I learned from another group of psychologists that the same therapist who does couples therapy shouldn't also do individual sessions with both members of the couples group. My last individual session and my last couples session with Eva took place several months after the first sessions, in which my partner and I understood that, according to her, "Eva," we were a lost cause.

After that last session, we didn't go back... I go to a psychologist because I need help, not so they can tell me our relationship is a lost cause. (They didn't say it like that, but that's how my partner and I understood it, and we never went back.)

Currently, we're still in couples therapy at another practice where individual and couples therapy aren't mixed. (They explained to us that it wasn't the right way to do things.)

Several years have passed, and we still have our disagreements. A few months ago, we went back to therapy at this new practice where they don't mix couples and individual therapy, and it's been a real eye-opener.

A few days ago, I found out that my partner told my wife (in our individual sessions) to give up on me and that we wouldn't end up together.

I live in a rented apartment, and after the washing machine broke down, the landlord bought a new one in Castromán. Two workers came to remove and install it: an older man and a young man, apparently an apprentice.

From the very beginning, the older worker ridiculed the young man for his weight, even saying he didn't know if the elevator could handle him. His behavior was simply shameful.
Once in the apartment, he didn't stop criticizing the state of the plumbing and the installations, insisting that everything was terribly done. When I wanted to see how the washing machine worked, it became clear he didn't know much about it. When I told him not to worry because I had the instruction manual, he became defensive and replied that he only worked with high-end washing machines and that the one he was installing was "the cheapest available." A rather unpleasant and completely unnecessary attitude.

To top it all off, after taking a picture of the washing machine, he suggested taking a picture of me, without explaining why, and with my daughter present. A very uncomfortable and totally inappropriate situation.

And to top it all off, when he gave me the delivery note to sign, he folded the document so that only the signature area was visible, completely obscuring the rest of the content.

In short: a grotesque experience, with an overbearing attitude, disrespect towards his colleague, and behavior that I found entirely unprofessional.

I mustered up the courage, swallowed my pride, and out of necessity, returned on August 26, 2026. You were very kind to me, and on August 27, I spent almost 45 minutes explaining everything over the phone. I began to believe in the power of psychology again; I saw hope. You told me to wait to schedule the appointment after discussing the problem with the team. Today is September 30th, and I called to confirm my suspicions. You neither knew about me nor remembered me. I'm not angry anymore, but I do feel immense sadness, and now, I'm not going back, because... you weren't the first to disappoint me either.

I'm happy for those of you who were helpful.

one_star_reviews.text:
We booked and prepaid a car for €95.10 through the Alamo website, using a physical Revolut Visa card. The booking was confirmed without issue.

On July 3rd, we went to the Puertollano AVE train station office to pick up the vehicle. The card was in the driver's name and had sufficient funds for the €200 deposit. However, the employee refused to use it as soon as he saw it was a Revolut card. He didn't attempt to process the deposit, and the card wasn't declined by the terminal; he simply told us they didn't accept Revolut.

This surprised us because the terms and conditions we received with the booking stated that they accepted physical Visa, Mastercard, and American Express credit or debit cards, and didn't mention any specific exclusion for Revolut.

We then called customer service three times. On the first two calls, they told us the refund had already been processed and would arrive in 10-15 days. We asked for an email or confirmation number, and they said they couldn't provide it. The money never arrived.

On the third call, weeks later, they told us for the first time that they wouldn't refund our money because we supposedly didn't meet a requirement and that there was a €150 penalty. We never received any written explanation.

We also sent a formal complaint by email and received no response.

Finally, we had to open a dispute with Revolut. Only after doing so did Alamo issue a refund of €95.10, and Revolut closed the case once they received the money.

We got our money back, but the service was terrible: contradictory information, no response to our written complaint, and no communication from the company throughout the entire process. I recommend carefully reviewing the payment terms before booking and keeping all documentation.

The best advice is not to use this service in Spain, as the Spanish make up rules that don't exist, and the customer service is so deplorable that you can't even reach an agreement with the person you speak to. If I hadn't opened a dispute with Revolut, Alamo would never have refunded the amount they charged me with the same VISA card that the station employee later refused to accept for the deposit. They're a disaster as a company and thieves.

Terrible is an understatement. I went there for a termination of pregnancy, and it felt more like I was going for a vehicle inspection than a clinic that treats people in vulnerable situations. Aside from the curt and almost inhuman treatment—not to mention the complete lack of it—it seems like the entire clinic staff is bitter about their jobs and life. I didn't even see the doctor who performed the procedure; I DIDN'T SEE OR GET TO KNOW THE DOCTOR! When they administered the sedation, I burst into tears from the pain caused by the anesthesiologist inserting the cannula. She didn't reassure me or speak to me at any point. I fell asleep sobbing uncontrollably, and when I woke up, the nurses abruptly and roughly took me to some suspicious beds because I doubt they even change the sheets.
In the room with the beds, there was a television playing a series that made absolutely no sense in an environment and situation like this. After a while, they gave me a pack of wipes to clean the blood from my vagina, which I had to throw on the floor because there was nowhere to put them.
YOU DON'T NEED TO RESPOND WITH THE TYPICAL MESSAGE OF "WE'RE SORRY FOR THE TREATMENT YOU RECEIVED AND WE'LL PASS ON THE MESSAGE," because you won't. This clinic is a dump, with staff who lack the necessary tools to deal with people in vulnerable situations. At my next appointment at my local health center, I plan to tell them to remove this clinic from the list so it can provide a proper public service. SHAMEFUL.

Today I went to get a vaginal Doppler ultrasound, and when I arrived the doctor told me they don't do them. How is it possible that the reception staff or the people in charge of providing information to the public don't know what tests are done at the clinic? They've made me waste my whole morning, because it's not just the travel but everything involved in attending a medical appointment.

1. My experience at this center was profoundly negative. I spent approximately a year and a half there, and personally, I feel it was a time in my life I will never get back.
2. During my stay, I experienced a constant feeling of sadness, helplessness, and lack of freedom. On many occasions, I had the impression that the center's rules and internal operations took precedence over the needs and well-being of the residents.

3. The food was another aspect that greatly disappointed me. I found the quality very poor, and there were situations related to portion sizes that caused me particular frustration and distress.

4. If you are considering admission, especially for a mild or moderate problem, I recommend researching beforehand, thoroughly understanding the conditions, and evaluating all available alternatives before making a decision.

5. One of the things that affected me most was the feeling of having no control over my own situation. I even counted the days until I could regain my independence and continue with my life outside the center.

6. This review reflects solely my personal experience. For me, it was a very difficult time and an experience I wouldn't recommend repeating. I hope my opinion helps others to be well-informed before making such an important decision.

My partner is 20 years old and was admitted to Pampuri on August 4th. He has a drug problem. The psychologist (Paula) has seen him only four times in 20 days, even though we were told he would have therapy every day. At the last session, she left him crying and went out to talk on the phone. The counselors are not qualified to do this job; they speak rudely to all the residents and don't care in the slightest about the mental health of the young people. The doctor isn't even a psychiatrist and hasn't even looked at him. One day his shoulder dislocated, even though he'd had surgery for it, and they gave him ibuprofen for three days, doubting his pain. Calling work therapy "work therapy" or labor exploitation is ridiculous. My partner asked for a bribe because he couldn't sleep until 3 a.m., and they refused to give it to him because otherwise he wouldn't get up for work. He ended up requesting to be discharged voluntarily, and they treated him with contempt, telling him he wasn't a role model and that he wouldn't be able to say goodbye to his family. Colleagues, two days after my discharge we asked for the reports and they completely ignored us, speaking to us with absolutely no respect. If you are or have a family member with drug addiction problems, don't go to Pampuri unless you want them to relapse or come out worse, because, in case you didn't know, they still bring in drugs and in 20 days not a single drug test has been done.

one_star_reviews.text:
I entered the shop with my two daughters, aged four and ten. They were checking a toy. The eldest daughter removed a sticker from the toy to demonstrate its workings to her younger sister. She then placed it back the toy with  the sticker . Suddenly, a seller approached her rudely, demanding payment and accusing her of miss using the toys . I was just three steps  away, getting some sunscreen, and returned to pay when I found my daughter crying.

Firstly, let’s consider the context. This is a shop in the airport where children come to see, and maybe if something gets their attention to buy  a  toy. She didn’t break anything; she didn’t remove it from a package, she did not brake it and she wasn’t alone for more than five minutes. Couldn’t the seller have waited a moment and approached me to explain what was happening? Instead, it was easier to come and make a child cry and accuse me of not educating my daughter properly. Seriously?  Please lady  change jobs because we’re customers with children in the airport’s kids’ section, and they didn’t exhibit inappropriate behaviour.

Please avoid coming to the duty-free shop, El Merecido. Give your money to someone else.

To the lady who intervened and said nothing happened:

Yes, nothing happened. I agree that nothing happened that I couldn’t have apologised for, paid for the toy, or adhered to the shop’s policy. But why did it happen? What happened is a bad experience and unnecessary use of power from an adult to a children…

To the male manager or colleague that talked to my daughter and tried to calm her …. thanks for your attention to us and kindness….

A few years ago, I went to see Sandra for my first and only appointment during a critical moment, suffering from severe depression and feeling utterly desperate.

Within minutes of speaking to her, her response was to call me a victim and tell me something along the lines of not giving her any of that nonsense. I left there completely devastated, having paid an exorbitant fee only to be cornered and coldly dismissed.

Both my doctor and colleagues from her own circle who know her were stunned by her attitude. Fortunately, I recovered thanks to cognitive-behavioral therapy with a professional who has genuine vocation and ethical rigor, the complete opposite of what I experienced there.

Now that I am fully recovered, I can assess what happened: a lack of empathy and clinical tact that, when dealing with patients in critical situations, is unacceptable. I am leaving this record to warn anyone seeking a safe therapeutic space.

one_star_reviews.text:
Very disappointed with the experience

Three months ago, we went to Mobilia to buy furniture and made it very clear from the outset: “WE CAME HERE BECAUSE THEY TAKE AWAY THE FURNITURE.” At no point were we informed that furniture removal had to be requested in advance, nor that it was a service managed by another company that they were supposed to notify.
The young man who helped us was friendly and helpful, so I won't mention his name, but there was a MAJOR oversight on his part in not informing us of something that was ESSENTIAL for us.

The most frustrating thing was that the day before delivery, when we had to go back to finish paying the remaining amount, we were informed that we had to have requested the removal of the old furniture beforehand. Something that, as I said, we had made clear from the very beginning.

The result? Today we were forced to make 80 trips to the recycling center to get rid of the furniture, with all the hassle and time that entails. And all because of a lack of information that we believe should have been provided at the time of purchase.

On the other hand, we were also disappointed by the supposed "gift" with our purchase. The woman who recommended us bought a sofa for around €1,600 and received a small gift from the company. We spent €3,600 on a bedroom set, and when we asked, we were told that they didn't receive anything from the warehouse. We're not asking for a gift, it's just that they treated some customers differently than others after making a purchase of that amount.

An experience that, frankly, has left us quite disappointed. We will not buy from Mobilia again, nor will we recommend the store to anyone.

However, we do want to highlight something positive: the men who came today to assemble the furniture were very kind, polite, and professional. They are not to blame for what happened and deserve to have their good work recognized.

My experience has been very disappointing. My mother went to this optician's to have sunglasses fitted, and at no point did they indicate that she might have cataracts or recommend an eye exam. Two days later, she went to an ophthalmologist for another reason, and he diagnosed her with cataracts, which were visible during the examination.
Today we returned to the optician's to inform them of what happened, and instead of acknowledging that it might have been overlooked, their response was to justify themselves by saying that a "special lens" is needed to see cataracts. This explanation surprised us greatly, since the ophthalmologist detected them immediately during the examination.
We understand that an optician is not a substitute for an ophthalmologist and is not obligated to diagnose illnesses, but we do expect that if a possible eye problem is detected or there are any doubts during an eye exam, they would recommend consulting a specialist before selling glasses. The service we received and the way they handled the situation have caused us to lose confidence in this establishment.

one_star_reviews.text:
Very bad experience with the service received.

My mother has been a GAES customer for some time, and her hearing aids were purchased at a GAES center in Valencia. When she lost one of them, we bought the new hearing aid at the same Valencia center where she had purchased the previous ones. Since my mother lives in the Caspe area, we went to the Alcañiz center for the necessary adjustment.

We were extremely surprised when the person who served us criticized us for having bought the hearing aid in Valencia, arguing that "they make the profit in Valencia, and she's the one who does the work," and told us that next time we should buy it directly in Alcañiz.

I consider it completely inappropriate to pass on internal issues regarding sales, profits, or the division of work between centers of the same company to the customer. If GAES offers a network of centers for the follow-up and maintenance of its customers, it shouldn't make the customer feel like they are bothering them by going to a different center than the one where they made the purchase.

The service we received was very unprofessional and made us feel extremely uncomfortable. It's one thing to have different internal centers and management systems, but quite another to hold the customer responsible for that.

I hope GAES reviews this type of service, because when someone pays a significant amount for a medical and everyday product, the least they expect is to receive professional and respectful treatment, regardless of where they made the purchase.

one_star_reviews.text:
Can an organization like SegurCaixa Adeslas afford to have a rating of 1.8, with 1 being the lowest? The problem isn't poor service; the problem is that they don't care. Let me tell you my story: My mother, an oncology patient at the Quirón Salud Hospital in Ciudad Real, needs a diagnostic test, in this case, a PET/CT scan. For this test, she has to travel to Madrid, with prior authorization from Adeslas. So, we went to the office to request the authorization, and from the list they offered, we chose Clínica de la Luz. At the same time, we contacted this clinic to schedule the appointment, and they told us that, since it's a nuclear medicine test, it has to be performed at the Quirón Hospital in Pozuelo de Alarcón. Nine days had passed since the authorization request, and there was still no word. So we went back to the Adeslas office, and they agreed to expedite the process. The authorization arrived two days later (eleven days total). Well, two days before the medical appointment at Pozuelo Hospital, they contacted my mother and told her that the authorization she had received wasn't valid because it was for the Clínica de la Luz. Good heavens! So, a third trip to the SegurCaixa Adeslas office ensued. The employees there offered to write an email, hoping that, by some miracle, the recipient, amidst the hundreds of messages in their inbox, would be kind enough to read it and change the authorization for the test she had to have the next day. Faced with this, I asked the employee why she didn't call, and she told me it was their protocol and she absolutely wouldn't do it. But, being so kind, she recommended that my mother (a cancer patient who needs a routine test that Adeslas doesn't offer in the province of Ciudad Real) travel to Madrid and find a SegurCaixa Adeslas office there to have the authorization changed. Given this absurdity, I called customer service, and an operator resolved the issue in five minutes, sending me the authorization by email. Once the test was done, it was time to request reimbursement for travel expenses. I'll tell you about that later, but I can tell you now that I had to go to the office SIX times to receive 29 euros.

one_star_reviews.text:
I went to this clinic for lip augmentation and ended up having an experience I honestly wouldn't wish on anyone.

I was very happy with the results of the first session. However, at the two-week follow-up appointment, the doctor insisted I needed more product. I trusted her professional judgment, because you go to a specialist expecting them to advise you correctly, not because you have medical knowledge to know what you need and what you don't.

After that second session, my lips swelled considerably, bruising appeared, and hard, very visible lumps formed. I was desperate about the appearance of my lips and contacted the clinic numerous times, even sending photos to show them what was happening. The response I received was basically that they thought it looked fine and that it was a normal reaction.

They offered me several radiofrequency sessions, but in my case, I didn't see any improvement. Despite continuing to express my concern, I didn't feel they understood the seriousness of the problem for me or that they were providing an effective solution.

Finally, when I insisted I couldn't continue like this, they suggested dissolving the hyaluronic acid with hyaluronidase, but at an additional cost.

The most frustrating thing is that I trusted the doctor's judgment and followed her instructions. I didn't expect a cosmetic treatment to be free of complications, but I did expect my concerns to be taken seriously and that I would receive care commensurate with the trust I had placed in them.

I believe that when a patient trusts a clinic, the least they expect is that the clinic will take responsibility for what happened and offer a suitable solution. I don't think it's fair to have to pay more to correct a problem that appeared as soon as I left the clinic, with excessive swelling and hard lumps in my lips. I'm sharing my experience because I wish I had known about it before going, and I think other people should know how these situations are handled at this clinic.

And, as if all this weren't enough, I still have to go to another clinic and pay another professional to try to remove the remaining hard lumps and restore the appearance of my lips. After everything that's happened, I have to shoulder even more expenses to try to solve the problem and feel comfortable and confident with my own lips again.

Stay away from this car rental company. They are unclear and unreliable. On the website, when you book online, it says "all inclusive" and "all covered" in the amount you'll pay for renting "X" car for "X" days.
However, you then discover hidden details, such as a €200 deductible that will be "blocked" and then "unblocked" upon return, and that the €200 extra deposit is for "the possible loss of the car keys." Upon return, they highlight existing scratches and dents, which are almost impossible to dispute since the videos and photos are taken under the scorching, strong sun that reflects off a clean car (see the photo).The curvature of the bodywork on the driver's side front fender was already present on the day the car was picked up... it is barely noticeable when the car is clean and was evident when the car was returned which, after 4 days of Saharan sand rain, was completely dirty with sand!).
When returning the car, the infamous scratches or small dents are also evident. This was the case with that small indentation on the left front fender.
Avoid this company at all costs, unless you want to ruin your vacation. People like this—who lack professionalism, operate with opaque contracts, and rely on deceiving their customers—will inevitably fail and end up right back where they belong.
Ps:I'm suing you for defamation. I'm writing to the Spanish prosecutor's office, the Majorca prefecture, and the consumer rights office.
If I get pissed off, I'll shut you down.
